title: At the Doctor: Describing How You Feel
summary: Learn how to talk about your body and health in English. Practice saying what is wrong when you go to the doctor.

sections.p: When you are sick, you can use the verb 'have' to talk about your pain or illness. We often use this with words like 'cold', 'headache', or 'stomachache'. It is very easy and useful. Listen to how people say it: 'I have a headache' means my head hurts. You can also say 'I have a fever' when your body is too hot.

ex.mean: She is sick with a cold.

sections.p: Another great way to describe pain is to use the word 'hurt'. Just say the part of your body first, and then add 'hurts'. For example, your leg, your arm, or your back. If the pain is in two places, we say 'hurt' without the 's'. For example, 'My legs hurt.' This helps the doctor know exactly where you feel bad.

ex.mean: I have pain in my arm.
I have pain in both eyes.

sections.p: When you visit a doctor, they will ask questions to help you. They might ask, 'What is the problem?' or 'How do you feel today?' You can answer simply using the phrases you learned. For example, 'I feel tired' or 'I feel sick.' The doctor will listen and then give you medicine to help you feel better.

ex.mean: What is your health like right now?

words.mean: person who helps you when sick
pill or liquid to get well

tip: Touch the part of your body when you say the English word. This connects the word to your physical feeling and helps you remember it faster!
